summary: France’s NDC excerpts combine EU-level and France-specific restoration, land-use, conservation and agriculture measures. For restoration, the EU-level objective is to put measures in place on at least 20% of EU land areas and 20% of its sea areas by 2030, with all ecosystems needing restoration addressed by 2050; peatland and wetland rewetting has a reported 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr mitigation potential. Biodiversity-respecting reforestation and sustainable forest management have a reported 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr potential. Conservation includes a collective EU LULUCF sink target of −310 Mt CO2-eq by 2030, representing 310 Mt of net removals and 42 Mt CO2-eq additional removals over the 2016–2018 average; France’s listed national 2030 target is −6,693 Kt CO2eq. Agriculture includes improving fertiliser-use efficiency, with a reported 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr potential. No French hectare allocation is stated; France’s 549,094 km2 land area has 2022 cover shares of 49.1% agriculture, 27.6% forest, 18.0% grassland and 0.3% wetland.

No French coverage area is stated; agriculture is 49.1% of France's 2022 land cover.
